checks.note: Dedicated ServiceAccount defined in serviceaccount.yaml; no other workload in the repo uses it, and the pod mounts its own projected token (audience sts.identity.example-corp.test).

ERP MCP, payments and Slack clients all call broker.token_for (mcp_client.py:119, payments.py:27, main.py:88). No client reads the incoming Authorization header or cookie; the user bearer is only used to authenticate /runs.

The user (principal.subject, main.py:155) is carried as a separate delegated subject while the workload token stays as the exchange credential. Caveat: the field mapping is non-standard (user in actor_token as a bare subject-id, agent as subject_token), and how the STS validates it is outside this repo.
The repo has a ServiceAccount but no RoleBinding, IAM policy or STS grants. Permissions and revocation for the principal are defined outside this repo.

note: A01.1-A01.3 hold in the code, but A01.4 cannot be confirmed because permission bindings and STS policy are not in this repo.
